facts.claim: Anthropic's multi-agent research post (June 13, 2025): its helpers work in parallel, each with its own context window, and hand the lead a condensed summary.
Anthropic (June 13, 2025): past 200,000 tokens its lead agent's context window is cut off, so the lead saves its plan to memory first.
Vendor-reported by Anthropic (June 13, 2025): agents use about 4× the tokens of a chat, and multi-agent systems about 15×.
Vendor-reported by Anthropic (June 13, 2025): a lead with helpers beat a single agent by 90.2% on its own internal research test.
Anthropic (June 13, 2025): to pay their way, multi-agent systems need tasks valuable enough to cover the extra cost.
Anthropic (June 13, 2025): without detailed task descriptions, its helpers duplicated work, left gaps, or failed to find what they needed.
Anthropic (June 13, 2025): tasks where every agent needs the same context, or with many dependencies between agents, are not a good fit for multi-agent systems today.
Anthropic (June 13, 2025): its lead waits for each set of helpers to finish, so the whole system can be blocked waiting on a single helper.
The A2A protocol (v1.0.0), for messages between agents: a message's parts are text, a file, or a block of structured data.
The A2A protocol (v1.0.0) names an error, ContentTypeNotSupportedError, for a message whose parts come in a type the receiving agent does not support.
Coffman, Elphick and Shoshani (1971): a deadlock needs a circular chain, each process waiting for something the next one holds.
Cemri et al. (2025): agents unaware of when to stop caused 12.4% of the multi-agent failures they studied.
Cemri et al. (2025) sorted the failures in over 1,600 runs of 7 multi-agent frameworks into 14 kinds, in 3 groups.
Cemri et al. (2025): missing or incomplete checks caused 8.2% of the failures they studied, and wrong checks 9.1%.
